text:
Midway through the second period in Chicago, the Jets were down 4-0, their starter had been pulled, and our win probability had them in single digits. They won 5-4 in a shootout. It was, as the Winnipeg Free Press' Ken Wiebe noted, the second time they have come back from four goals down, and along the way Mark Scheifele became the franchise's all-time points leader.

Chicago could hardly have played the first half better. Tyler Bertuzzi scored 1:48 in, rookie Anton Frondell tipped in a second, and Connor Bedard scored on a power play with four seconds left in the first, set up by Patrick Kane. That chased Stuart Skinner after three goals on eight shots. Frank Nazar made it 4-0 on another power play at 14:44 of the second.

Then Scheifele took over. He scored at 16:05, set up Kyle Connor's slap shot two minutes later (a 1% chance, and Connor's 700th career point), and assisted on Cole Perfetti's power-play goal 55 seconds into the third. Winnipeg owned that period on chances, 1.64 expected goals to 0.45, and with 1:13 left Gabriel Vilardi tied it, the goal that moved the Jets from a 7% win chance to 48%. Spencer Knight stopped Vilardi on a 35% look in overtime to keep Chicago alive, but Scheifele and Connor both scored in the shootout and Kane's goal wasn't enough.

The quiet hero was Nico Daws, who came on cold and stopped 12 of 13. By our measure he added more to the win than anyone. Scheifele finished with four points in 25 minutes, Josh Morrissey played almost 33, and Winnipeg out-shot Chicago 31-21 and won this game in 66% of our replays. That's six straight wins for the Jets. The Blackhawks, whose coach Jeff Blashill needed Bedard's public backing during a recent losing run, will hate this one.
headline: Scheifele's record night caps a four-goal Jets comeback
